chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ubayd Allah al-Dihqan from Musa ibn Ibrahim from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the sale of fodder and grazing land, so he said, 'There is no objection to it; the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) enclosed al-Naqi' for the cavalry of the Muslims.'

key_terms.النَّقِيعَ: Al-Naqi', a specific location near Medina
key_terms.الْكَلَإِ: Fodder or dry grass used as animal feed
key_terms.لِخَيْلِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: For the cavalry of the Muslims

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell grazing land and fodder in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, where Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the commercial transaction of fodder and grazing lands by citing the Prophetic precedent of enclosing al-Naqi for the Muslim cavalry. This hadith establishes the juristic principle that public or communal resources can be designated for exclusive private or institutional use, thereby legitimizing their sale and ownership in Shia fiqh.
